title: Dead earth, dead hearts, dead bones: He brings them to life
subtitle: Al-Muhyi: the Giver of life to bodies, to the earth and to hearts
intro: Al-Muhyi (الْمُحْيِي) means The Giver of Life: the One who gives life to a lifeless drop and makes it a living person, revives dead land with rain, brings hearts to life with faith, and will raise the dead. Every heartbeat you have is His gift. And no part of you, or your faith, is too dead for Him to revive.

root.sense: Hayah is life, and ihya' is to give life or revive. It is the same root as Al-Hayy, the Ever-Living. He is living in Himself, and from that perfect life He gives life to others. The word is also used for reviving land, and for a heart coming alive.

picture.label: Three kinds of life He gives

knowing: Life is the one thing no laboratory can produce. Science can describe the parts of a body in detail, yet give a scientist flesh and bone and ask for a living person, and nothing can be done. {idea}Al-Muhyi is the only Giver of life{/idea}: He proportions the body and then breathes the soul into it (15:29), a thing whose reality He has kept mostly hidden from us (17:85).

His giving life flows from His own life. He is Al-Hayy, the Ever-Living who never dies, and all His actions, giving, protecting, sustaining, come from that perfect life. Whatever lives, lives because He gives it life at every moment.

The Quran uses this name for three kinds of life. The body in the womb. The earth after rain. And the heart: is one who was dead, then We gave him life and a light to walk by among people, like one stuck in darkness (6:122)? {reward}Faith is called life, and its absence is called death{/reward}.
seeing: A man passed a ruined town and wondered how Allah could ever bring it back to life. Allah caused him to die for a hundred years, then raised him. His food had not spoiled, but his donkey had turned to bones, and he watched them being assembled and clothed with flesh. His words afterwards: I know that Allah has power over all things (2:259). Right after, Ibrahim asked to see how Allah gives life to the dead, not from doubt but so that his heart would be at rest (2:260).

You can watch the same sign every year. Look at the traces of Allah's mercy: how He gives life to the earth after its death; that same One will give life to the dead (30:50). And in Surah al-Hadid, straight after warning believers not to let their hearts harden, Allah says: know that Allah gives life to the earth after its death (57:16-17). {reward}The message to a hard heart is: rain is coming{/reward}.
trusting: Some seasons of faith feel like winter ground. You pray and feel nothing. The Quran that once moved you sits on the shelf. {trap}You conclude that something in you has died for good{/trap}. Al-Muhyi revives land that looked like it would never grow again. Keep the small seeds in the ground, a little Quran, a little dhikr, a dua, and ask Him for rain.

The same hope applies to a child who has drifted, a friend who has lost faith, a marriage that feels lifeless. You cannot breathe life into anything. He can, and He responds to those who ask. Respond to Allah and His Messenger when he calls you to what gives you life (8:24).
loving: Every morning you did not choose to wake up; your life was handed back to you. {reward}Each breath is a fresh gift from Al-Muhyi{/reward}, given without asking. The heart that notices this cannot help but love the One who keeps giving it life.
now: You are sitting in the car outside the mosque, engine off, unable to make yourself go in because it has felt empty for months. Al-Muhyi brings dead ground to life after rain. Go in anyway, pray two rak'ahs, and ask Him for the rain your heart needs.
old: When my faith feels dead, I assume it is over for me.
new: Al-Muhyi revives dead land and dead hearts, so I keep planting and ask Him for rain.
try: Read one page of the Quran slowly today, even if you feel nothing, and treat it as a seed you are planting for Al-Muhyi to water.

dua.text: Ya Muhyi, You give life to the earth after its death. Give life to my heart with faith and Your remembrance, and do not let it harden.
dua.note: Call on Him by this name when your heart feels hard or empty, and for anyone whose faith you long to see revived.

pairs.why: He gives life and He causes death; both are in His hand, and the Quran mentions them together.
He gives life because He is the Ever-Living whose life has no beginning and no end.
Al-Muhyi gives life; Al-Ba'ith raises the dead from their graves on the Day of Resurrection.

faq.a: Al-Muhyi means The Giver of Life. Allah gives life to the body by creating it and breathing the soul into it, to the earth by sending rain, to the heart by guiding it to faith, and to the dead at the resurrection.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Hayy and Al-Muhyi?
faq.a: Al-Hayy describes Allah Himself as the Ever-Living, whose life is perfect and never ends. Al-Muhyi describes His action of giving life to others. He gives life because He is living, and no created thing lives without Him.

faq.q: Are Al-Muhyi and Al-Mumit mentioned together in the Quran?
faq.a: Yes, many times. Verses such as 2:258, 3:156, 15:23, 40:68 and 57:2 say that Allah gives life and causes death, often together with His power over all things or His dominion over the heavens and earth.
